title: Metabolic biorthogonal labeling and dSTORM imaging of peptidoglycan synthesis in Streptococcus pneumoniae
protocol: Prepare fresh CY medium.
Thaw a 50-μL aliquot of a frozen glycerol stock of pneumococcal cells.
Inoculate 1 mL of CY medium with the glycerol stock (starting OD600nm = 0.1).
Incubate the culture for 90 min in a 15-mL Falcon tube at 37°C in a static CO2 incubator.
Dilute the culture by adding 9 mL of CY medium to 1 mL of culture.
Further incubate the diluted culture at 37°C until the OD600nm reaches 0.3.
Dilute the culture again by mixing 1 mL of sample with 9 mL of CY medium (starting OD600nm = 0.03).
Incubate the second dilution at 37°C until the OD600nm reaches 0.3.
Pre-warm fresh CY medium, aDA-DA solution, and PFA at 37°C.
Centrifuge the culture at 4,000×g for 15 minutes at 22°C.
Resuspend the cell pellet into 1/25th volume of CY medium.
Mix 200 μL of the cell sample with 50 μL of 10 mM aDA-DA to achieve a final concentration of 2 mM.
Incubate cells for 5 minutes at 37°C in a water bath.
Fix cells by adding 260 μL of PBS-PFA 4% to the 250-μL sample.
Incubate for 12–18 hours on ice at 4°C.
Incubate for 15 min at 37°C in a water bath (CHASE period).
Centrifuge the fixed sample at 7,000×g for 5 min at 22°C.
Resuspend the cell pellet into 150 μL of PBS 1× and 10 μL of 500 μM DIBO-AF647.
Incubate for 1 h at 22°C in the dark (CLICK reaction).
Add 1 mL of 1× PBS to the sample.
Wash twice by centrifuging the cell sample at 7,000×g for 5 min at 22°C.
Resuspend the cell pellet into 1 mL of 1× PBS.
Evaluate the fluorescent signal-to-noise ratio by conventional fluorescence microscopy before proceeding to dSTORM data collection.
Prepare the dSTORM buffer during the two washes.
Centrifuge the cell sample (7,000×g, 5 min, 22°C) and resuspend the pellet into 15 μL of dSTORM buffer.
Load 8 μl of cell suspension onto a rectangular UV-treated microscopy coverslip.
Place a square coverslip onto the cell drop.
Place a Kimtech wipe on top.
Apply a 2.3-kg weight onto the coverslip for 15 minutes to allow cells to settle on the microscopy slide.
Place and remove the weight by applying a precise vertical movement to prevent slipping of the coverslip.
Seal the setup with transparent nail polish.
Optional: Replace the nail polish with twinsil silicon glue.
Optional: To orient the cells vertically relative to the microscopy coverslip, load 300 μL of 2% (w/vol) agarose solution onto a rectangular UV-treated microscopy coverslip.
Place a micropillar device horizontally on top of the agarose drop and wait for about 30 minutes until the agarose has solidified.
Remove the micropillar device as vertically as possible and cut the excess agarose around the microholes.
Prepare the dSTORM buffer without GLOX solution approximately 40 minutes before the end of the fluorescent tagging step.
Load 20 μL of dSTORM buffer without GLOX on the agarose pad.
Incubate for 10 minutes at 22°C and remove excess buffer.
Load 15 μL of cell suspension onto the agarose pad.
Apply a slow circular movement to spread the cell suspension all over the agarose pad.
Let the agarose pad sit for 10 min at 22°C.
Wash twice with 10 μL of dSTORM buffer containing GLOX.
Do not flush into the microholes but rather apply a horizontal flow at the surface of the agarose pad.
Place a square UV-treated coverslip on top of the agarose pad.
Immobilize the coverslip with two pieces of tape.
Place an autofluorescent pink slide on top of the objective.
Set up the 643-nm laser at low intensity.
Orient the laser vertically relative to the slide (epifluorescence illumination).
Center the laser in the camera field of view.
Place an autofluorescent yellow slide on top of the objective.
Set up the 405-nm laser at low intensity and center it in the camera field of view to overlap with the 643-nm laser.
Position the sample so that the rectangular coverslip is oriented toward the objective.
Find a concentrated but non-overlapping field of cells and acquire a bright-field image.
Set up the 643-nm laser at 0.5% intensity (8.5 W⋅cm−2).
Adjust the focus and acquire a diffraction-limited fluorescence image.
Progressively increase the 643-nm laser intensity from 0.5 to 100% within about one minute.
Acquire the dSTORM image stream using 100% intensity of the 643-nm laser and an exposure time of 50 ms, with EM gain set at 200 when fluorophores start blinking.
Progressively increase the intensity of the 405-nm laser from 0.1 to 3% (0.05–1.5 W⋅cm−2) as needed to maintain a constant blinking frequency.
Adjust the exposure time so that the ON time of each fluorophore covers a single frame.
Set the EM gain to cover the dynamic range of the camera.
Analyze the acquired dSTORM frames using the NanoJ-SQUIRREL plugin for initial experiments.
Plot the resolution versus the number of frames from the analysis.
Estimate the optimal number of frames based on the plateau phase of the curve.
Clean the leftover immersion oil on the objective before placing a new sample.
Apply a new drop of immersion oil after cleaning.
Divide the number of detected photons by the camera Quantum efficiency.
Check the emission spectrum of your dye before referring to the Quantum efficiency graph.
Calculate the pixel size of the camera using an image of a microscope ruler taken with a 100× oil objective.
Take a brightfield image of a calibration target slide, such as R1L3S2P from Thorlabs.
In ImageJ select the "Straight line" tool.
Plot a cross-section profile ("Analyze" → "Plot profile").
Measure the distance between the furthest visible lines of the ruler.
Divide the known distance in micrometers by the measured value in pixels to calculate calibration.
Prevent any light from entering the camera (e.g., by closing a shutter).
Set exposure time to 0 ms and record a stack of 100 images.
Go to "Analyze" → "Set Measurements".
Check that the "Mean grey value" parameter is selected.
Make an ROI of the image size.
Add the ROI to ROI manager ("Analyze" → "Tools" → "ROI manager" → "Add").
Select your ROI from the list and click "More" → "Multi Measure".
Calculate the base level as the mean of the 100 obtained values by clicking "Results" → "Summarize".
In ImageJ, calculate the mean intensity of each image using "Analyze" → "Measure".
Average the two mean intensity values.
Using the "Image Calculator" tool ("Process" → "Image Calculator"), subtract one image from another.
Check both boxes to create a new window and use 32-bit (float) result.
Go to "Analyze" → "Set Measurements" and ensure that the "Standard deviation" parameter is selected.
Measure the standard deviation of the resulting image using "Analyze" → "Measure".
Calculate the variance from the standard deviation: Var = StdDev^2 / 2.
Calculate the photon conversion factor (PCF) using values from steps 27, 28b and 28e: PCF = (Average_1 - Base level) / Var.
Repeat previous steps with a few more exposure times (e.g., 10, 20, 40 ms).
Launch the ThunderSTORM plugin under FIJI.
Open the Camera set up window and specify the "Pixel size", "Photoelectron count”, "Base level" and "EM Gain" values found in the certificate of camera performance or equivalent document.
Adjust the "Peak intensity threshold" value if needed, starting with a default value between 0.5 and 2 to correct for false positive or negative localizations.
Specify the "Fitting radius" value determined previously.
Round up decimal values of the fitting radius.
Specify "Maximum likelihood" as the "Fitting method".
Enter an "Initial sigma" value approximated to one third of the "Fitting radius" value.
Select "Normalized Gaussian" as the visualization method.
Run data analysis.
Plot the "Sigma" parameter using the "Plot histogram" tab.
Calculate the "Initial sigma" value as the ratio between the "Mean" value of the sigma distribution and the "Pixel size" value.
Enter the new "Initial sigma" value in the "Sub-pixel localization of molecules" parameters.
Run the analysis again.
Plot the "Uncertainty_xy" value using the "Plot histogram" tab.
Note the localization precision as the "Mean" value of the uncertainty distribution.
Correct the drift by choosing "Fiducial markers" in the "Drift correction" tab if fiducial markers were used during data acquisition.
Otherwise, use the "Cross correlation" method to correct the drift.
Use fiducial markers when cells are trapped between two coverslips.
Correct drift using the cross correlation method when cells are trapped in microholes.
Ensure that few fiducial markers are present in the field of view.
Check that all fiducial markers display the same drift.
Generate the final reconstructed dSTORM image through the "Visualization" tab.
Filter out multi-emitters by their Sigma value using the "Filter" tab.
Remove background noise using the "Density filter" tab.
Combine multiple localizations of the same molecule with the "Merging" function.
